story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
### AC-1: GET /api/users Endpoint - List Users with Pagination - Paginated list with tenant_id, is_active, role filters - Query params: tenant_id, is_active, role, limit (default 20, max 100), offset - Response includes user details with roles array - RBAC: super_admin sees all, tenant_admin scoped to their tenant
### AC-2: POST /api/users Endpoint - Create New User - Validates email (RFC 5322), password strength (8+ chars, 1 upper, 1 lower, 1 number, 1 special) - Validates default_tenant_id exists, initial_role is valid RoleEnum - Returns 201 Created with user details - Side effects: bcrypt hash, initial role assigned, AuthAuditLog entry, welcome email sent
### AC-3: PUT /api/users/{id} Endpoint - Update User - Updates email, is_active, default_tenant_id (all optional) - Validates cannot disable last active super_admin - Validates cannot update self if disabling - Authorization: super_admin updates any, tenant_admin only their tenant users - Side effects: AuditLog entry with changed_fields
### AC-4: DELETE /api/users/{id} Endpoint - Soft Delete User - Soft delete (is_active = false), not hard delete - Cannot delete self or last active super_admin - Side effects: revoke JWT refresh tokens, remove all role assignments, AuditLog entry - Returns 204 No Content
### AC-5: POST /api/users/{id}/reset-password Endpoint - Admin Password Reset - Generates secure 16-char temp password - Sets force_password_change = true - Revokes all refresh tokens - Returns temporary password (shown once), sends email - AuthAuditLog entry created
### AC-6: Tenant Isolation Enforced - super_admin: no automatic scoping - tenant_admin: scoped to users with roles in their tenant (user_tenant_roles.tenant_id filter) - Applies to all endpoints
### AC-7: Audit Logging for All Operations - AuditLog table: create, update, delete operations - AuthAuditLog table: user_created, admin_password_reset events - Captures: entity_type, entity_id, action, changed_fields, performed_by, tenant_id, timestamp, ip_address, user_agent
### AC-8: Input Validation and Error Responses - 400 Bad Request with Pydantic validation errors - Password rules: min 8, 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 number, 1 special (!@#$%^&*), no whitespace - Email: RFC 5322 format, case-insensitive uniqueness, lowercase normalized

story-context.constraints: 1. **RBAC Enforcement**: All endpoints require `@require_role("super_admin", "tenant_admin")` decorator 2. **Tenant Isolation**: super_admin = no filtering, tenant_admin = filter by user_tenant_roles.tenant_id 3. **Password Security**: Use bcrypt hashing, validate strength (min 8, 1 upper, 1 lower, 1 number, 1 special), never log plaintext 4. **Audit Logging**: Every modification → AuditLog entry, auth events → AuthAuditLog entry, capture changed_fields JSON, IP address, user agent 5. **Error Handling**: 400 (validation), 403 (permissions/scoping), 404 (not found), 409 (email conflict). Use FastAPI exception handlers. 6. **Service Layer Pattern**: API routes thin (HTTP concerns), service layer thick (business logic, DB ops, audit logging) 7. **Testing Standards**: Unit tests (mock DB), integration tests (test DB), 80%+ coverage target, MUST test RBAC enforcement 8. **File Size**: All files ≤500 lines. Split if needed per Project Constraint C1. 9. **Code Quality**: Black formatter, Mypy strict type checking, Bandit security scan 10. **Soft Delete Only**: DELETE endpoint sets is_active=false, NOT hard delete from database 11. **Last Super Admin Protection**: Cannot disable or delete last active super_admin in system 12. **Email Async**: Use Celery tasks for welcome email and password reset email (non-blocking)

tests.standards: Follow existing Pytest + pytest-asyncio patterns from tests/unit/ and tests/integration/. Use AsyncMock for database mocking in unit tests. Use test database with transactions for integration tests. All async test functions must use @pytest.mark.asyncio decorator. Black formatting, type hints, comprehensive docstrings required. Target 80%+ coverage on new code. CRITICAL: Test RBAC enforcement (super_admin vs tenant_admin access) for each endpoint.

tests.ideas: - **AC-1 Tests**: list_users with different roles (super_admin sees all, tenant_admin scoped), pagination, filters (tenant_id, is_active, role) - **AC-2 Tests**: create_user validates email uniqueness, password strength (all 5 rules), assigns initial role, sends welcome email, returns 201 - **AC-2 Error Tests**: Invalid email format (400), weak password (400), duplicate email (409), invalid tenant_id (404) - **AC-3 Tests**: update_user prevents disabling last super_admin (400), logs audit entry with changed_fields, tenant_admin cannot update outside their tenant (403) - **AC-4 Tests**: delete_user soft deletes (is_active=false), prevents self-deletion (400), prevents deleting last super_admin (400), revokes JWT tokens, removes role assignments - **AC-5 Tests**: reset_password_admin generates secure password, sets force_password_change=true, revokes tokens, sends email, creates AuthAuditLog entry - **AC-6 Tests**: Tenant scoping logic - super_admin can access all users, tenant_admin only sees users in their tenant, tenant_admin cannot access other tenants' users (403) - **AC-7 Tests**: Audit log entries created for all operations (create, update, delete, password_reset), IP address and user agent captured - **AC-8 Tests**: Password validation rejects weak passwords (missing uppercase/lowercase/number/special, < 8 chars, whitespace), email validation rejects invalid formats
